_: CANONICAL CHECK REGISTRY. Every checker in the production verification pipeline appears here exactly once, with the exact line that wires it into each engine. parity.js asserts this list and the two shipped pipelines agree in BOTH directions, so a checker added to production and not registered here fails the suite; negative-control.js drives its removals from this list, so registering a checker is what puts it under negative-control coverage. Edit the pipelines and this file together.

checks.name: exhaustion
checks.note: Reads the domain the question sets (positive/non-negative/distinct integers) and rejects a claimed value outside it; then, for P = c^(linear form) only, PROVES a bound on the search region by induction in exact integer arithmetic and enumerates that region whole. Emits nothing when the bound cannot be proved — a bounded search is not a completeness proof.

checks.name: sequenceCheck
checks.note: Checks a named sequence against the terms actually written. The case it exists for is 1, 1, 2, 5, 13 — every OTHER Fibonacci number, which the Markov equation produces — where the recurrence is a(n) = 3a(n-1) - a(n-2) and calling it Fibonacci gets the indexing and the next term wrong.

checks.name: counterexample
checks.note: Hunts for a value that refutes a universal claim the answer made — a primality, a sign or parity, or an inequality asserted for every value. It can only ever FAIL: a clean search is not a proof and must never be reported as one, so a claim it cannot refute is left to unproved(), which asks whether an argument was given.

checks.name: stepChain
checks.note: Walks the working line by line and compares consecutive equations by SOLUTION SET. A step may gain solutions (squaring does) but may never lose one: dividing 2x^2 = 6x by x loses x = 0, every later line is still true, and substitution passes the answer. Corroborating, because a sound derivation of the wrong thing is still wrong.

checks.name: unitmath
checks.note: Carries MAGNITUDE as well as dimension, which the frozen Units table deliberately does not: 60 km/h = 21 m/s and F = 5 kg x 2 m/s^2 = 10 J are both invisible to a dimension-only check. Temperature is an offset scale, not a factor. Reads a line only when BOTH sides carry units it knows, and refuses an unknown unit rather than guessing.

checks.name: sigfigs
checks.note: Advisory: an answer quoted to nine figures from data measured to one is over-claimed, and it costs marks. Reads only numbers that carry units — a coefficient in an equation is not a measurement — and needs three more figures than the data before it says anything.

checks.name: directionCheck
checks.note: Advisory: a one-directional step (squaring, clearing a denominator, dividing by an expression) incurs the debt of substituting every candidate back, and this reports the debt unpaid. It reads prose, so it may never decide the badge; substitution is what actually catches an extraneous root.

checks.name: optimality
checks.js: try { if(!extremum.length) checks = checks.concat(optimality(question, text)); } catch(e){}

_limits: The pipeline-to-registry sweep in parity.js recognises the two ordinary wiring shapes (a result concatenated directly, or parked in a local declared with it). Checkers wired unusually — inside a ternary, or assigned to a pre-declared local — are invisible to it and carry a note here. Wire new checks the ordinary way and the sweep will catch a missing registration for you.
